validity_findings.finding: Branching stochastic FSM eliminates ceiling as designed. H(S_next|URL,H_K=3)=1.533 bits (MTO) /1.537 bits (UNIQ) >0.2 bits threshold. Recomputed from raw_result.json:conditional_entropy matches result.json. Strata (63 at K3) have genuine next-state uncertainty.

BC PMI MTO K3=0.225711 bits (observed 0.27813 - perm_mean 0.052419), Bonferroni p=0.0 (0/1000 perms >= observed, *4 corrections). Recomputed matches producer. Primary threshold C2 (BC>0.05 and p<0.0125) passes independently of C3. Same for UNIQ K3=0.493481 bits.

Frozen falsifier clause 2 / decision rule C3 (mto < uniq -0.1 => aliasing was sole source / FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING) is conceptually misaligned. Difference -0.2677 triggers FALSIFIED label, but sole-source would require mto≈0, not just -0.1 drop. Producer correctly reports mto 0.226 bits remains >0.05 and significant; therefore 45.8% of uniq signal persists. FALSIFIED label per frozen rule is arithmetically correct but scientifically overbroad; it quantifies aliasing as SIGNIFICANT not SOLE source.

baseline_findings.finding: Unique-content baseline (S0≠S1≠S2, 3 hashes) yields BC PMI 0.493 bits at K3 (0.565 at K1) with same FSM/sessions. Recomputed difference -0.268 bits (54% reduction) quantifies aliasing contribution. Baseline is strong within-experiment comparison and correctly implemented with identical session_directions table.

State-independent baseline (constant response) not explicitly computed as separate condition; positive control (randomized state→content) serves as functional equivalent with BC≈0 (0.0019). Spec baseline expectation BC≈0 validated.

Action-history-only ceiling eliminated via conditional entropy H=1.53 bits. No explicit accuracy baseline P(S_next|URL,H_K) reported, but H>0.2 threshold exceeds spec. Would strengthen to report majority-class accuracy vs 33% frequency baseline.

Finite-sample bias demonstrated: permutation null mean 0.052 bits (MTO K3) and 0.107 bits (UNIQ K3). BC correction (obs-perm_mean) used consistently for primary and controls. Null control confirms BC mean ≈0 under permutation. Estimator baseline is valid.

claim_ceiling: On locally-hosted 3-state stochastic branching FSM (states S0,S1,S2, actions advance/branch, session-direction p_left=0.7/p_right=0.3, URL=/app, N=20 sessions seed 42, 200 trajectories*10 steps=2000 transitions per condition), response-content PMI I(S_next;Response_before|URL,H_K=3) is 0.226 bits (BC, Bonferroni p=0.0 <0.0125, H>0) when S0 and S1 share content (2 hashes) vs 0.493 bits when all states unique (3 hashes). The 0.268-bit drop (54%) demonstrates content-state aliasing is a significant source of prior PMI, but residual 0.226 bits >0.05 shows content retains partial state information (S2 isolated vs {S0,S1} partition) sufficient for significant PMI. This does NOT demonstrate fully content-independent predictive dynamics, does NOT test fully-ambiguous (1 hash) case, and does NOT generalize beyond this synthetic Express SPA with hash-based observation, p=0.7/0.3 independent per-transition stochasticity, and no production DOM/auth/latency. Maximum justified is partial discrimination, not emergent dynamics beyond memory.
unresolved: Does residual 0.226 bits reflect genuine response-context transition information or solely partial state discrimination (S2 vs {S0,S1})? Requires fully-shared 1-hash condition where Response is invariant to state.

Would PMI persist with correlated non-deterministic transitions (session state, external data) where Response_before correlates with latent environment state determining S_next, rather than independent per-step observation noise?

Generalization to production SPAs with client-side rendering, auth-dependent content, and richer DOM/accessibility representations remains untested; synthetic-to-real gap is dominant unknown for C-WEB-DYNAMICS.
Stability of difference estimate to larger N and alternative history encodings (e.g., learned embeddings vs exact action-sequence strata) not measured.
Whether action-sequence non-identity across conditions (RNG sequencing) biases difference estimate materially, despite identical session_directions table.
